lead: Tesla / TSLA — Musk is back in charge
smaller: Strategy / MSTR — bitcoin treasuries are the new buyback
D-Wave / QBTS — buy the quantum dip
Silver / SLV — the cheaper gold trade
why_lead: TSLA closed at 288.14 USD on the prior session with a five-session gain of 27.89%, the largest move of any megacap in the market data, after a 20-session decline of 4.84% against a reference close of 302.80. The same-period attention headlines (Fortune on Musk being back in charge after an all-hands meeting, TradingView on a retail buying frenzy, Cathie Wood's $2,600 target) coincide with that move, and the story is simple enough for the crowd to repeat. Tariff leeway reported by Reuters gives the rebound a concrete catalyst.
why_smaller: Strategy's five-session gain of 20.70% and 20-session gain of 36.45% are backed by the GameStop bitcoin-treasury plan and Metaplanet's 150-bitcoin addition, so the treasury narrative is the repeatable story.

QBTS fell 18.70% over five sessions after a 48.31% gain over 20, and the headlines split between buy-the-dip calls and CEO scepticism about practical quantum use, a dip-buying narrative distinct from bitcoin.

Silver futures are up 6.92% over 20 sessions and SLV up 6.07%, with a commentary calling silver higher-upside than gold, a non-equity metals trade that is separate from the bitcoin and quantum narratives.
considered_not_chosen: Carvana (CVNA, five-session gain of 33.11%) and AppLovin (APP, five-session gain of 24.19%): large moves, but the same-window attention evidence is thin and the stories are not simple.
Robinhood (HOOD, five-session gain of 20.07%): attention centres on brokerage products and a Massachusetts regulatory probe rather than a price-led crowd thesis.
Trump-linked stablecoin and token ventures: strong attention, but no listed instrument with a card price in this window; the venture is covered in the crypto section instead.
Nuclear names (OKLO, five-session gain of 11.18%): real news flow, but the story is contract and regulatory, not the crowd's simple thesis.

Rheinmetall (RHM.DE, 20-session gain of 38.49%, five-session fall of 8.72%): a sharp dip, but the attention headlines are about German defence spending rather than retail trading, so it is not carried into the retail section.
Gold futures and gold miners: the silver trade already carries the bullion backdrop, and a second precious-metals pick would repeat the same basket.
Copper: a record-high tariff headline and a 15.54% 20-session gain, but there is little retail-attention evidence, so copper is used in the underowned themes instead.
No earlier retail selection notes existed in this sandbox, so the editorial-memory comparison could not be made against prior dates.
